subject: System Design
title: How Twitter Designed Its Timeline
description: A 60-second lesson on How Twitter Designed Its Timeline.

hook.text: You open Twitter and see tweets from 500 people you follow, sorted by time. Building that feed is surprisingly hard.

buildup.text: Early Twitter pulled tweets at read time: query every followed user, merge, sort. At scale, this was too slow.

discovery.text: Twitter switched to fan-out on write: when you tweet, it's pushed into every follower's pre-built timeline cache.

twist.text: 50M-follower celebrities make fan-out expensive. Twitter uses a hybrid: fan-out for most, pull for celebrities.

climax.text: The timeline is a classic example of how the same problem needs different solutions at different scales.

punchline.text: Fan-out on write for most, pull on read for celebrities.

quiz.question: Why does Twitter use a hybrid approach for timelines?
options: Fan-out is too expensive for users with millions of followers
Pull on read is always faster
Caching doesn't work for social media
